turns.user_message: We're finalizing registration for the Summer Splash Reading Program at Maplewood Public Library. Can you help me work out the age-group cutoffs and participant caps for each tier?
turns.assistant_message: For the Summer Splash Reading Program, Director Renata Hollis has proposed three registration tiers: Ages 4–7 (Early Readers), Ages 8–12 (Middle Readers), and Ages 13–17 (Teen Readers). Coordinator Jamie Osei confirmed participant caps of 120 for Early Readers, 150 for Middle Readers, and 80 for Teen Readers, giving a total program cap of 350 registered participants. Registration opens June 2, 2024, and the Program Guide 2024 lists these caps as firm limits subject to staff-to-participant ratios.

turns.user_message: What prize structure has been discussed for participants who complete the reading goals in the Summer Splash Reading Program?
turns.assistant_message: Director Renata Hollis approved a three-tier prize structure for the Summer Splash Reading Program: participants who log 5 books receive a Maplewood Public Library bookmark set and a certificate, those who log 10 books earn a $10 bookstore gift card, and those who log 15 or more books receive a $25 gift card plus a trophy. Coordinator Jamie Osei noted that ReadTracker Pro will automatically flag accounts when thresholds are crossed so prizes can be distributed without manual review. The total prize budget allocated in the Program Guide 2024 is $4,800 for the full summer.

turns.user_message: Has a decision been made about which software platform will handle reading logs for the Summer Splash Reading Program?
turns.assistant_message: Maplewood Public Library selected ReadTracker Pro as the official reading-log platform for the Summer Splash Reading Program after a three-vendor review completed on March 15, 2024. The annual license fee is $1,200, and Coordinator Jamie Osei will serve as the primary system administrator with two backup logins assigned to reference staff. ReadTracker Pro supports parent-managed accounts for children under 10, which Director Renata Hollis identified as a key requirement in the Program Guide 2024.

turns.user_message: What's the staffing plan for running the Summer Splash Reading Program events at Maplewood Public Library this summer?
turns.assistant_message: Coordinator Jamie Osei drafted a staffing plan that assigns two full-time staff members per weekly program event, supplemented by four trained volunteers per session. Director Renata Hollis approved a volunteer recruitment target of 20 volunteers total for the Summer Splash Reading Program, with an orientation session scheduled for May 28, 2024. The Program Guide 2024 specifies that at least one certified children's librarian must be present at every Early Readers session held at Maplewood Public Library.

turns.user_message: I need to figure out the marketing plan for promoting the Summer Splash Reading Program. What channels and timeline has been discussed?
turns.assistant_message: Director Renata Hollis and Coordinator Jamie Osei agreed on a four-channel marketing plan for the Summer Splash Reading Program: social media posts beginning May 1, flyers distributed to 12 local elementary schools by May 10, a press release to the Maplewood Gazette on May 15, and an email blast to the Maplewood Public Library newsletter list of 3,400 subscribers on May 20. The Program Guide 2024 sets a marketing budget cap of $600 for printed materials and paid social boosts. ReadTracker Pro's landing page will also feature a registration link starting May 1.

turns.user_message: For the prize structure, has anyone confirmed how the $10 and $25 gift cards will be sourced — local vendor or national chain?
turns.assistant_message: Coordinator Jamie Osei confirmed at the April 3 planning meeting that all gift cards for the Summer Splash Reading Program will be purchased from Hartwell Books, a local independent bookstore two blocks from Maplewood Public Library. Director Renata Hollis supported the local vendor choice, noting it aligns with the library's community partnership goals and that Hartwell Books agreed to provide a 5 percent discount on bulk gift-card purchases over $500. The Program Guide 2024 records Hartwell Books as the sole approved vendor for prize fulfillment.

turns.user_message: Does the prize budget of $4,800 account for the Hartwell Books discount, or is that the pre-discount figure?
turns.assistant_message: According to Coordinator Jamie Osei's budget notes reviewed on April 10, the $4,800 prize budget for the Summer Splash Reading Program is the post-discount figure, already reflecting the 5 percent reduction from Hartwell Books. The pre-discount total would have been approximately $5,053, so the library saves roughly $253 through the partnership. Director Renata Hollis confirmed this in writing to the Maplewood Public Library finance office on April 12, citing the Program Guide 2024 line item for prizes.

turns.user_message: Has ReadTracker Pro been tested yet for the Summer Splash Reading Program, and are there any known issues with the platform?
turns.assistant_message: Coordinator Jamie Osei ran a pilot test of ReadTracker Pro on April 18, 2024, using 15 test accounts across all three age tiers of the Summer Splash Reading Program. Two issues were found: the parent-managed account feature showed a login timeout after 8 minutes of inactivity, and the book-search database was missing roughly 200 titles published after January 2024. ReadTracker Pro's support team committed to patching both issues by May 9, 2024, and Director Renata Hollis was notified via the Program Guide 2024 issue tracker.

turns.user_message: For the staffing plan, how many hours per week is each full-time staff member expected to dedicate to Summer Splash Reading Program duties?
turns.assistant_message: Coordinator Jamie Osei's staffing plan, approved by Director Renata Hollis on April 5, 2024, allocates 8 hours per week per full-time staff member to Summer Splash Reading Program duties during the program's 8-week run from June 10 to August 2. This includes 3 hours of event facilitation, 3 hours of ReadTracker Pro account management and prize tracking, and 2 hours of parent and patron communication. Maplewood Public Library's HR office confirmed these hours fall within existing contracts and require no overtime authorization.

turns.user_message: What is the overall budget for the Summer Splash Reading Program, and who approved the final figures?
turns.assistant_message: Director Renata Hollis presented the final Summer Splash Reading Program budget to the Maplewood Public Library board on April 22, 2024, and it was approved at $18,500 total. The budget breaks down as $4,800 for prizes, $1,200 for the ReadTracker Pro license, $600 for marketing, $7,900 for staffing and volunteer coordination, and $4,000 for programming supplies and author visits. Coordinator Jamie Osei was named budget manager, responsible for tracking expenditures against the Program Guide 2024 line items throughout the summer.

turns.user_message: Has a final decision been made on which schools will receive the Summer Splash Reading Program flyers, and is there a contact list?

Director Renata Hollis approved the list and authorized printing 50 flyers per school, for a total print run of 750 flyers at a cost of $187.50, within the $600 marketing budget.

turns.user_message: How many total registered participants did ReadTracker Pro show for the Summer Splash Reading Program pilot test on April 18?

These 15 pilot accounts are separate from the actual program caps of 120, 150, and 80 participants approved by Director Renata Hollis.

turns.user_message: Has the $18,500 total budget for the Summer Splash Reading Program been broken down further for the $7,900 staffing line?
turns.assistant_message: Coordinator Jamie Osei provided a staffing sub-breakdown in the April 22 budget document: $5,600 covers the proportional salary cost for two full-time staff at 8 hours per week over 8 weeks, $1,500 covers volunteer stipends and training materials for 20 volunteers, and $800 is reserved for contingency overtime at Maplewood Public Library. turns.user_message: For the school outreach, has Maplewood Public Library confirmed whether teachers can assign Summer Splash Reading Program participation as optional summer homework?
turns.assistant_message: Director Renata Hollis contacted the Maplewood Unified School District office on April 29, 2024, and received confirmation that teachers may recommend the Summer Splash Reading Program as optional summer enrichment but may not assign it as graded homework under district policy 7.4.2. Coordinator Jamie Osei updated Appendix C of the Program Guide 2024 to include this caveat so school contacts would not misrepresent the program to families. The library will provide each school with a one-page FAQ sheet clarifying the voluntary nature of the program and the ReadTracker Pro sign-up process.

turns.assistant_message: Coordinator Jamie Osei conducted a follow-up test of ReadTracker Pro on May 12, 2024, confirming that the login timeout had been extended to 30 minutes of inactivity and that 198 of the 200 missing post-January 2024 titles had been added to the database. turns.user_message: For ReadTracker Pro, what happens if a participant's account shows a disputed book log — is there an appeal process?

When a dispute flag is raised, the case is routed to the Maplewood Public Library admin account, where a staff member reviews the entry and either approves or rejects the log within 5 business days. Director Renata Hollis approved a policy, recorded in the Program Guide 2024, that a brief written summary from the participant is required for any dispute involving a title not found in the ReadTracker Pro database.
